value.summary: For the two-use half-skew BSSC, restrict to the four deterministic product-code orientations and vary only the 16 positive masses q(W,X^2). At the tensor square of the exact one-use randomized-time-division optimizer, entropy differentiation gives a constant gradient on all cells. Restricting the exact Hessian to the 15-dimensional simplex tangent space and applying an exact LDL^T decomposition over Q(sqrt(105)) yields 15 strictly negative pivots. The interior second-derivative test therefore proves a strict local maximum of the half-weight Marton functional within this fixed-map quotient.
value.title: Exact local-curvature proof for the fixed product-code quotient

value.summary: A Python standard-library checker constructs the governed product channel, four fixed auxiliary orientations, tensor-product mass law, and seven entropy marginal maps. Working exactly in Q(sqrt(105)), it verifies the tensor law, all 15 tangent gradient log-product identities, Hessian symmetry, the 15 strictly negative LDL^T pivots, and exact matrix reconstruction without using floating-point arithmetic for the governing predicates.
value.title: Exact product-code quotient curvature verifier

value.summary: In the 15-dimensional quotient formed by fixing the four stated deterministic product-code orientations and varying only the positive masses q(W,X^2), the tensor product of the exact one-use randomized-time-division optimizer is a strict local maximum of L_{1/2}, with value 2L_RTD. Because the selected-law Marton value is at most L_{1/2}, every distinct sufficiently close law in this quotient has selected-law Marton value below 2L_RTD. This local result does not exclude distant points, activation of other atoms, stochastic or different maps, larger auxiliaries, gains in other architectures, unrestricted Marton nonadditivity, or a capacity improvement or converse.
value.title: Strict local maximum in the two-letter product-code quotient

placementAudit.rationale: The accepted theorem rigorously prunes the local geometry of a fixed two-letter Marton product-code architecture around repeated randomized time division. It directly advances the existing objective of identifying which product and correlation structures can or cannot yield a multiletter Marton gain, without changing the broader program hierarchy.
